items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1959-06-02
items.q: Frankie Duesen wasn't a good reader. But he had a good ear.

ctx.x: No. But he had a good ear. See? He played mostly by the... Frankie Duesen wasn't a good reader. But he had a good ear. See? Poor ear. At the time he was... He wasn't a good reader. But I believe he picked up there. I think he reads pretty well now, they say. I believe.

The question, Risley, I've had this formal education in playing trombone in concert bands, in marching bands. But I'm always playing set notes of music, something that somebody else has written for me. And I'm very enchanted by this Dixieland music where the trombone player seems to be making it up and improvising and playing things that aren't written. And the music is a very happy type of music, which I think is good for relaxation for lawyers, among other people. And I'm wondering, how do you play, what do you…

Well, at our time back there, you know, we wasn't much of a reader. Spellers, and the trombone, he didn't do much. Most of the time he had bass licks, you know. And then he had nod, then he'd have a little solo or something. But he didn't play trombone like those fellas. The most was a gift, and we done most sliding and faking on such an audible step, you see. We couldn't play no trombone like those boys were playing that they didn't know how. You see, and which was just mostly a gift. And most of us played from…

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-11
items.q: That's like Bob Lyons and Frankie Deucing.

ctx.x: Well, you tell me you did go to school that while. But you might have done here. Mm-hm. If this sounds like an old-time band that you know of, the style that they're playing in…

That's like Bob Lyons and Frankie Deucing. That's like Bob Lyons and Frankie Deucing. Yeah, that's way back there. That's the old style way back on the center. They might not be an old musician, but it's sound.
Well, they're old. But that was only made about a year ago.
